brewing.notes: A safe starting point for oolong: gongfu style with water just off the boil.

description:
A Fenghuang dancong from Guangdong described by its origin in population stock.

This is a tea plant cultivar rather than a finished tea, so you are more likely to meet its name in a grower's notes than on a packet. If you find tea made from it, brew it like any other oolong tea and taste what the plant brings.
history: One Fenghuang aroma line of this stock is said to come from trees that temple monks planted in the early Qing. In the summer of 1958 a production team captain found the failing old tree and saved the type with short cuttings. Little more is documented.
processing: A plant cultivar, not a processing style: it is usually made into oolong tea, and the method is up to the grower.
harvest_season: Depends on the place and the grower.
appearance_dry: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
appearance_liquor: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
appearance_wet: Depends on how the leaf is processed.
taste_profile: Depends on how the leaf is processed; tea from it usually falls within what oolong teas give.
vintage_note: A cultivar is not sold by vintage. Tea made from it follows the usual pattern for oolong tea, so ask for the harvest year and the grower.
